Verdict: REVISEThe Section 6 unequal-scale theorem is mathematically sound under the inherited canonical model:nearest-neighbor grid edges; $M$ -edges are the charged “actual” edges;each actual edge has unit cost in the displayed equalities;a full matching  $N$  decomposes  $M\cup N$  into vertex-disjoint alternating terminal paths and doubled  $M$ -edge cycles;feasibility for  $T$  means that  $T$  is monochromatic/independent and each selected  $T$ -vertex has at most one neighboring  $P$ -vertex.I found no counterexample to the all- $(K,\ell)$  construction under those premises. The required changes are document-level but should be made before acceptance because the current text leaves the parity/feasibility convention and cost normalization implicit, and one row-range sentence is incorrect for unequal scales.The supplied archive contains the note as docs/HH_SOURCE_BUDGET_AND_FORCED_FLOW_OVERPAY.md; it does not contain the separately named core source files such as SOURCE_OWNERSHIP_FEE_SANDWICH.md. Thus the review below treats the earlier core lemmas as premises, as requested, rather than independently certifying those missing source files.1. Section 6 counts are correctPut
$$s=K+\ell.$$
The board dimensions are
$$(4K+4\ell+2)\times(4K+4\ell+4)
=(4s+2)\times(4s+4),$$
so
$$\frac{\operatorname{area}}2
=\frac{(4s+2)(4s+4)}2
=8s^2+12s+4.$$
Each odd core of scale  $a$  has  $(4a+1)^2-1$   $P$ -vertices and therefore
$$\frac{(4a+1)^2-1}{2}=8a^2+4a$$
matching edges. Hence
$$|M|
=8K^2+4K+8\ell^2+4\ell
=8(K^2+\ell^2)+4s.$$
With the intended parity assignment,  $Q$  has equal odd and even populations because the board has even-by-even dimensions and  $P$  is itself matched. The claimed values
$$|T|=16K\ell+8s+3,\qquad
|H|=16K\ell+8s+5$$
therefore give
$$|T|+|H|=32K\ell+16s+8=|Q|.$$
The area quantity is
$$J=|M|+|T|
=8(K^2+\ell^2)+16K\ell+12s+3
=8s^2+12s+3,$$
and hence
$$J=\frac{\operatorname{area}}2-1.$$
So the “area deficit one” statement is correct for every  $K\geq \ell\geq 1$ .2. The parity and feasibility statement must be made explicitThe phrase“Retain  $z=(4K,4K+1)$  as the only white  $H$  and select every other white  $Q$ ”is too ambiguous for a proof. Replace it by an explicit parity definition. For example, with
$$\chi(r,c)=r+c\pmod 2,$$
write
$$Q_{\mathrm{odd}}
=\{q\in Q:\chi(q)=1\},\qquad
Q_{\mathrm{even}}
=\{q\in Q:\chi(q)=0\},$$
and define
$$T=Q_{\mathrm{odd}}\setminus\{z\},\qquad
H=Q_{\mathrm{even}}\cup\{z\}.$$
If the core source uses the opposite names “black” and “white,” reverse the labels, but state the parity convention explicitly.With this definition: $z=(4K,4K+1)$  has odd parity; $z\in H$ ;every other odd-parity  $Q$ -vertex lies in  $T$ ;every even-parity  $Q$ -vertex lies in  $H$ ; $z$  is the only odd-parity  $H$ -vertex.The geometric claim about the shared corner is correct. The point  $z$  is adjacent to the two core-corner  $P$ -vertices
$$(4K,4K)\in S_1,\qquad
(4K,4K+2)\in S_2.$$
No other odd-parity  $Q$ -vertex is adjacent to  $P$ -vertices from both cores. All other selected  $T$ -vertices have at most one  $P$ -neighbor. Since all  $T$ -vertices have the same parity,  $T$  is independent.There is one important dependency here. The full rectangle contains outside strips where selected  $T$ -vertices have zero  $P$ -neighbors. Therefore the proof is valid only under the inherited feasibility condition “at most one  $P$ -neighbor.” If the missing core source instead requires every selected  $T$ -vertex to have exactly one  $P$ -neighbor, the construction as written is not feasible and would need a substantive redesign. The note should state the convention directly.A suitable replacement sentence is:Feasibility in this model means that  $T$  is independent and every  $t\in T$  has at most one neighbor in  $P$ . The outside-strip  $T$ -vertices have zero  $P$ -neighbors, which is permitted; the only  $Q$ -vertex with two  $P$ -neighbors is  $z$ , and  $z\notin T$ .3. The universal TH lower bound is correctThe two centers are
$$h_1=(2K,2K),\qquad
h_2=(4K+2\ell,\;4K+2+2\ell).$$
They are both even-parity  $H$ -vertices, isolated in  $Q$ , and lie in distinct cores.Every terminal path in the alternating decomposition has opposite-parity endpoints. Therefore a path ending at either center must begin at an odd-parity endpoint. The only odd-parity  $H$ -endpoint is  $z$ . Consequently:a center can be on an  $HH$  path only if that path uses  $z$ ;both centers cannot simultaneously be on  $HH$  paths;the source  $z$  has capacity one because the terminal paths are vertex-disjoint.For arbitrary rematching of  $P$ , every  $T$ -to- $h_1$  path has Manhattan distance at least
$$2K+1,$$
so, because the path alternates  $N$ - and  $M$ -edges and has odd length, it contains at least  $K$  actual  $M$ -edges.Likewise every  $T$ -to- $h_2$  path has distance at least
$$2\ell+1$$
and therefore at least  $\ell$  actual  $M$ -edges.With unit actual-edge costs, the capacity-one source-budget theorem gives
$$f(N)\ge K+\ell-\Delta.$$
There is only one admissible odd- $H$  source,  $z$ , so its maximum possible discount is at most
$$\Delta\le \max\{K,\ell\}=K.$$
Thus, for every full matching and every rematching of the same  $P$ -footprint,
$$f(N)\ge K+\ell-K=\ell.$$
This correctly avoids the invalid argument that independently credits the same  $z$  to both centers.The source-budget proof also correctly respects resource capacity:different terminal paths are vertex-disjoint;hence their actual  $M$ -edge sets are disjoint;the same  $H$ -source cannot be assigned to two  $HH$  endpoints;the matching relaxation computes an upper bound on the total HH discount, not a simultaneous realization of independently shortest routes.That distinction should be stated explicitly because the theorem is a lower bound under arbitrary rematching, not a general exact optimizer.4. The canonical L-shaped completion attains  $f=\ell$ For the displayed canonical matching  $M=M_1\cup M_2$ , the left relay is
$$z,\ (4K,4K),\ (4K-1,4K),\ldots,(2K,4K),\
(2K,4K-1),\ldots,(2K,2K)=h_1.$$
It has: $4K+1$  grid edges; $2K$  actual  $M_1$ -edges; $z$  and  $h_1$  as its two  $H$ -endpoints.The first and last edges are  $N$ -edges, and the internal edges alternate between  $M_1$  and  $N$ . Since  $z$  occurs at even index  $4K$  on the first  $L$ -boundary, deleting  $z$  leaves two even-length boundary segments. Pairing those segments and doubling the unused  $M_1$ -edges gives the canonical full completion of  $B_1$ .For the second core, the translated straight relay should be written explicitly. Its  $T$ -endpoint is
$$t_2=(4K+4\ell+1,\;4K+2+2\ell),$$
and its center endpoint is
$$h_2=(4K+2\ell,\;4K+2+2\ell).$$
This is the translation by  $(4K,4K+2)$  of the scale- $\ell$  relay from the core construction. It has: $2\ell+1$  grid edges; $\ell$  actual  $M_2$ -edges;a selected  $T$ -endpoint  $t_2$ ;an even boundary index  $6\ell+2$  on the translated  $L_2$ .Deleting  $t_2$  leaves two even segments, so the same  $L$ -completion applies.The two completion blocks are vertex-disjoint because their column intervals are disjoint:
$$B_1=[0,4K+1]\times[0,4K+1],$$

$$B_2=[4K,4K+4\ell+1]\times[4K+2,4K+4\ell+3].$$
They overlap in two rows but not in vertices. The actual relay edges belong to different  $M_i$ , so they cannot overlap.The explicit TH-optimal completion uses:the  $2K$ -edge  $HH$  relay  $z\to h_1$ , which is free for  $f$ ;the  $\ell$ -edge  $TH$  relay  $t_2\to h_2$ ;direct  $TH$  boundary pairings elsewhere;doubled unused  $M_i$ -edges inside the two blocks.Therefore the displayed canonical  $M$  has a full matching with
$$f=\ell.$$
Combined with the universal lower bound, this proves
$$f^*=\ell$$
for the canonical matching.The note already intends the correct rematching distinction: the lower bound holds for every rematching of the  $P$ -footprint, while the equality  $f^*=\ell$  is an attainment statement for the displayed canonical  $M$ . That distinction should be retained and made more prominent.5. The unequal-scale row-completion sentence contains an actual parameter typoThe current Section 6 text says:“Outside the two blocks, each row consists either of the right  $n$ -column interval (rows  $0..4k-1$ ), no vertices (rows  $4k..4k+1$ ), or the left  $n$ -column interval (rows  $4k+2..8k+1$ ).”This is the equal-scale description and is wrong for general  $K,\ell$ . It uses  $k$  where both  $K$  and  $\ell$  are needed, and the lower range  $4K+2,\ldots,8K+1$  is generally incorrect.Replace it with:Outside  $B_1\cup B_2$ , the remaining vertices are:
$$\begin{array}{ll}
0\le r\le 4K-1:
& c=4K+2,\ldots,4K+4\ell+3,\\[2mm]
4K\le r\le 4K+1:
& \text{no remaining vertices},\\[2mm]
4K+2\le r\le 4K+4\ell+1:
& c=0,\ldots,4K+1.
\end{array}$$
The first leftover interval has width  $4\ell+2$ , the second has width  $4K+2$ , and both are even. Pair each interval horizontally.This is enough to complete the board. Every outside pair is a direct  $Q$ -to- $Q$   $TH$  pair under the explicit parity definition above.6. The all-terminal minimizer argument is correctFor the all-terminal objective  $C$ , use the two straight  $TH$  relays, and pair  $z$  directly with its neighboring  $H$ -vertex on  $L_1$ . The direct  $HH$  pair has zero actual  $M$ -edge cost. This gives a full matching with
$$C\le K+\ell.$$
Conversely, consider any full matching.Both centers are  $TH$ The center paths contribute at least
$$K+\ell$$
actual edges to  $C$ . $h_1$  is  $HH$ The only possible odd- $H$  source is  $z$ . The distance is
$$d(z,h_1)=4K+1,$$
so the  $HH$  path contains at least  $2K$  actual  $M$ -edges. The other center must be  $TH$ , contributing at least  $\ell$ . Thus
$$C\ge 2K+\ell>K+\ell.$$
 $h_2$  is  $HH$ Again the path must use  $z$ , and
$$d(z,h_2)=4\ell+1,$$
so it contributes at least  $2\ell$  actual  $M$ -edges. The other center is  $TH$  and contributes at least  $K$ . Therefore
$$C\ge K+2\ell>K+\ell.$$
The strict inequalities hold because  $K,\ell\ge1$ .Hence
$$\Phi=\min_N C(N)=K+\ell,$$
and every  $C$ -minimizer must put both centers on  $TH$  paths. For every such minimizer,
$$f(N)\ge K+\ell$$
from the two center paths, while  $f(N)\le C(N)=K+\ell$ . Therefore
$$f(N)=K+\ell$$
for every all-terminal minimizer, independently of tie-breaking.Thus the claimed family does establish
$$f^*=\ell,\qquad
\Phi=K+\ell,\qquad
f(N_C)=K+\ell$$
for every  $C$ -minimizer  $N_C$ , once the unit-cost convention and feasibility definition are stated.For  $\ell=1$ ,
$$f^*=1,\qquad
f(N_C)=K+1,$$
so the ratio
$$\frac{f(N_C)}{f^*}=K+1$$
and the additive overpayment  $K$  are unbounded while the area deficit remains one.7. Unit-cost normalization is requiredSection 1 allows arbitrary nonnegative edge weights  $w$ , but Section 6 writes literal integer equalities
$$f^*=\ell,\qquad \Phi=K+\ell.$$
Those equalities are valid only when every actual  $M$ -edge has unit cost, or when  $f$  and  $C$  are explicitly defined as counts of actual  $M$ -edge occurrences.Add a sentence at the beginning of Section 6:From this point through the remainder of the section, every actual  $M$ -edge has unit cost, and  $f$  and  $C$  denote the corresponding actual-edge cardinalities. The weighted source-budget theorem in Section 1 remains valid for arbitrary nonnegative weights, but the displayed exact values  $f^*=\ell$  and  $\Phi=K+\ell$  are the unit-cost specialization.Without this sentence, the section mixes a weighted lower-bound theorem with unweighted exact values.8. Resource use is sound, but should be statedThe canonical construction does not double-spend resources: $M_1$  and  $M_2$  are disjoint because the cores are separated by the gap column;the two completion blocks are disjoint in vertices;the left  $HH$  relay uses only  $M_1$ -edges;the right  $TH$  relay uses only  $M_2$ -edges;each unused  $M_i$ -edge is doubled only inside its own block;outside horizontal pairs use no  $M$ -edges;the source  $z$  belongs to only one terminal path.Add one sentence making this explicit:The two relay paths use disjoint actual  $M$ -edge sets, every unused  $M_i$ -edge is doubled at most once within its own block, and no outside horizontal pair meets either block; hence no actual resource is charged twice in the terminal-path decomposition.The finite JSON is useful as local consistency evidence, but it cannot establish the all- $(K,\ell)$  claim. The written distance, parity, capacity, and completion arguments are what support the theorem.The result does not contradict any numerical  $5/6$ , half-area, or related coloring target. It preserves
$$J=\frac{\operatorname{area}}2-1$$
and concerns only the mismatch between the all-terminal objective  $C$  and the TH objective  $f$ .
